findings.problem: TC-08 enumerates three deterministic fault locations but its oracle collapses them to 'provider has zero or one outcome'. That oracle can pass an invalid branch: after-admission-before-gateway and pre-SQLite-commit must prove zero provider outcome/effect, while post-SQLite-commit-before-ack must prove exactly one durable replayable outcome. The oracle also does not explicitly require every post-admission uncertainty branch to leave Knora executing with the same admission/logical ID/fingerprint and the typed indeterminate_external_outcome.
findings.required_change: Make TC-08 branch-specific. Require exactly zero provider ledger/effect for the before-gateway and pre-commit branches, exactly one durable replayable ledger outcome/effect-or-closed-rejection for the committed-before-ack branch, and in every not-yet-finalized post-admission branch assert lifecycle=executing, the unchanged admission/logical ID/fingerprint, and the exact indeterminate_external_outcome projection. Preserve zero retry/replay/takeover authority.

findings.problem: The contract requires request_fingerprint to be server-computed from the exact canonical-json-v1 operation/capability/scope/reference/target/normalized title-description intent, and requires both fingerprint and logical execution ID to be immutable and never caller inputs. Existing tests prove persistence, propagation and provider-side recomputation, but none independently proves the original server computation or that application/HTTP callers cannot supply or influence either identity.
findings.required_change: Add a required application/HTTP plus store oracle that independently recomputes the expected canonical-json-v1 fingerprint from authoritative normalized inputs, compares it with proposal/acquisition/admission/envelope/provider values, proves the logical execution ID and fingerprint are absent from writable caller input or rejected if injected, and proves both remain immutable across the complete generation-1 path.

findings.problem: The exact contract requires temporary execution-authority denial to leave the immutable proposal approved, while material capability/binding/policy/reference incompatibility must make it stale and require a new proposal and human approval. TC-01 only asserts the denial, absence of execution artifacts and zero provider calls; it does not observe the required post-denial proposal/approval state. A system that leaves materially incompatible approval reusable could therefore pass TC-01.
findings.required_change: Extend TC-01 with durable before/after proposal and approval state assertions: temporary execution-authority denial must preserve approved state unchanged, while every material incompatibility class must produce the exact stale/invalidation state that prevents later reuse and requires a new proposal and human approval.

findings.problem: AC-09 explicitly requires sanitized public projections and EV-06 names a sanitized public result matrix, but TC-10's application/HTTP oracle checks status/result mappings without an allowlist or forbidden-field assertion. TC-11's exclusion oracle applies to the canonical audit projection, not the public application/HTTP responses. EV-06 can therefore be claimed without a required Test Case that fails on public leakage.
findings.required_change: Add an explicit application/HTTP oracle, preferably to TC-10, that compares the complete public projection against its allowed schema for every success, closed rejection, indeterminate, conflict and fenced result and asserts absence of raw provider IDs/routing handles, envelope bytes/MAC, key or credential material, authority secrets and all other private admission fields.

summary: Revision 7 directly closes the three named external-review-v6 Major classes and preserves the sole deep WriteProposalWorkflow.handle Interface, generation-1-only boundary, static typed registry, and Issue #78 ownership of reconciliation/takeover/retry. Four independent required-oracle gaps remain, so the zero-finding approval condition is not met.
